stem: A client with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation is prescribed apixaban. Which statement about the labeled adult dose-reduction criteria is accurate?

options.A: Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of these criteria are present: age 80 years or older, body weight 60 kg or less, or serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or greater.
options.B: Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily whenever any degree of renal impairment is documented, regardless of age or body weight.
options.C: Keep the dose unchanged because age, body weight, and serum creatinine do not affect labeled NVAF dosing.
options.D: Increase the dose whenever serum creatinine reaches 1.5 mg/dL because lower renal clearance requires more drug to maintain effect.

rationale: Current ELIQUIS labeling recommends 5 mg twice daily for most adults with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation and 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of three criteria are present: age 80 years or older, body weight 60 kg or less, or serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or greater. A is correct.
educational_objective: Apply the labeled apixaban NVAF dose-reduction rule: 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of the three specified age, weight, and serum-creatinine criteria are present.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
source_locator: §2.1 Recommended Dose in Adult Patients: NVAF usual dose 5 mg twice daily; reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of age ≥80 years, body weight ≤60 kg, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL are present.
source_claim_supported: For adult NVAF, apixaban dose reduction to 2.5 mg twice daily is based on the presence of at least two of the three labeled age, body-weight, and serum-creatinine criteria.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: medication dosage/administration, adverse effects, monitoring and safe medication care.

source_original.stem: A client with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation is prescribed apixaban. Which statement about the labeled adult dose-reduction criteria is accurate?

options.A: Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two labeled NVAF dose-reduction criteria are present
options.B: Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily whenever any degree of renal impairment is documented clinically
options.C: Keep the dose unchanged because age, weight, and serum creatinine never affect NVAF dosing
options.D: Increase the dose whenever serum creatinine reaches 1.5 mg/dL because renal clearance is lower

source_original.rationale: For stroke and systemic embolism prevention in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, the current ELIQUIS label recommends 5 mg twice daily for most adults and 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of three criteria are present: age at least 80 years, body weight at most 60 kg, or serum creatinine at least 1.5 mg/dL. The prior item was too broad because apixaban dosing is indication-specific and renal impairment alone is not the universal rule described there.
source_original.source_detail: Current label version 38, section 2.1: NVAF dose 5 mg twice daily; reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of age ≥80 years, body weight ≤60 kg, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL are present.

correction_summary: Retained key A, expanded the labeled criteria directly into the keyed option, preserved indication-specific scope to NVAF, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item applies a direct three-criterion label rule.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed ELIQUIS version 38; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item exactly states the two-of-three labeled dose-reduction rule and avoids generalizing renal impairment alone across indications.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because any degree of renal impairment alone is not the labeled NVAF reduction rule.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because age, body weight and serum creatinine explicitly determine dose reduction when at least two criteria coexist.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because elevated creatinine does not trigger a dose increase.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reproduces the labeled NVAF criteria.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern the same dose-adjustment decision and use comparable wording.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication dosing and monitoring.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read ELIQUIS version 38 §2.1, all options, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
